clips.title: The story
paras: In Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof guards his people and Mulgore. While Cairne leads from Thunder Bluff, Baine directs local defense against gnolls and outside threats.

Baine Bloodhoof grew up traveling with his nomadic people, the son of Cairne. They settled in Mulgore’s grasslands, where centaur clans remained a threat. After the Third War, Khiragg’s warband captured Baine, and grief left Cairne nearly unable to lead the new settlements. Rexxar freed Baine from captivity. The rescue restored Cairne’s spirit, and the tauren stood with Thrall’s Horde against the invading Kul Tirans, securing their foothold on the continent.

Baine lives among his kin in Bloodhoof Village rather than at the capital mesas. As Cairne grows older, Baine bears more responsibility for the people and represents the next generation of tauren leadership. He directs braves and visiting allies against Palemane gnolls that trouble the borders, and watches for outside influences that threaten Mulgore’s natural balance.

Baine faces encroachers who give little thought to spiritual balance. East of Mulgore, the goblin Venture Company cuts into the sacred landscape. Dwarven prospectors from Bael Modan dig ancestral soil at the Bael'dun Digsite. Baine urges a firm but measured response: warn the miners and destroy their equipment instead of rushing into needless bloodshed. He says their violent digging hurts the spirits of the earth, but the miners refuse to listen.
